# Sogou Network Popular Words Auto-Update Tool

This project automatically downloads internet trending new words from the Sogou Pinyin input method dictionary and converts them into plain text format and YAML format usable by the Rime input method.

Note: This project was continuously iterated using vibe coding in April 2026.

## Features

- Automatically downloads the latest internet trending new words from the Sogou Pinyin input method dictionary
- Converts Sogou cell dictionary format (.scel) to plain text format (.txt)
- Generates two dictionary versions: the current version and the accumulated version (including historical entries)
- Preserves original SCEL pinyin mappings to avoid recalculating historical entries in the accumulated dictionary
- Converts dictionaries to YAML format usable by the Rime input method
- Daily automatic updates via GitHub Actions

## File Structure

```
.
├── .github/workflows/   # GitHub Actions workflow configuration
│   └── update_dict.yml  # Workflow for automatically updating the dictionary
├── data/                # Stores dictionary data
│   ├── sogou_network_words_current.txt        # Ground-truth word set for current version (plain text)
│   ├── sogou_network_words_accumulated.txt    # Ground-truth word set for accumulated version (plain text)
│   ├── sogou_network_words_current_pinyin.tsv # Pinyin mapping for current version (original SCEL pinyin takes priority)
│   ├── sogou_network_words_accumulated_pinyin.tsv # Stable pinyin mapping for accumulated version (historical entries frozen)
│   ├── luna_pinyin.sogoupopular.current.dict.yaml  # Current version dictionary (Rime format)
│   ├── luna_pinyin.sogoupopular.dict.yaml     # Accumulated version dictionary (Rime format)
│   └── version_info.json  # Version info
├── scripts/             # Script files
│   ├── download_and_convert.py  # Downloads and parses SCEL, writes txt/tsv ground truth
│   ├── convert_to_rime.py       # Generates Rime YAML from txt + tsv
│   ├── repair_pronunciation_data.py  # One-time fix for pinyin data in the current repository
│   └── run_all.py               # Runs all workflows
├── requirements.txt     # Dependency list
└── README.md            # Project description
```

Cross-platform VPN client for the **CSQTT** protocol. A single Flutter UI, platform backends in Rust / Kotlin / Swift, with support for desktop, mobile devices, and OpenWRT routers.

LaLune is a blocking-circumvention client based on the [CSQTT](https://github.com/Endlad2/csqtt-core) protocol. Traffic is disguised as VK Calls, TURN is used for NAT traversal, WRAP is used for encryption, and obfuscation hides the signature.

|---|---|---|---|
| Windows | ✅ | Flutter + Rust (axum) + Wintun | `client-windows-x86_64.exe` |
| Linux | ✅ | Flutter + Rust (axum) + TUN | `client-linux-x86_64` |
| Android | ✅ | Flutter + Kotlin + VpnService | `libclient-android-*.so` |
| iOS 17+ | ✅ | Flutter + Swift + NetworkExtension | `csqtt-core` (static lib) |
| OpenWRT | ✅ | Rust (axum) + TUN | `csqtt-client-aarch64` |

chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.body:
# ⚽ Football Signal Radar · Daily Signal Report

> **Set emotions aside, watch only the signals.**
> Cross-validation of line movements across three channels: no bets at low odds, no bets when signals are unclear. Pre-match bets are placed automatically; post-match settlement is automatic.

## 🚀 Live Site

- **[https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/](https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/)**
- Updated automatically every hour; historical dates archived for review at any time
- Covers **500–1,300+** matches per day (full 竞彩 and Asian handicap coverage), automatically flagging signals and bets

---

## Detours We Took

We tried **models**: piled on parameters until the room was full. Looking back, the model merely recited prices the market had already set. No matter how many parameters, it could not produce anything new.

We tried **studying the bookmakers**: guessing at the house's moves, guessing more and growing more paranoid. The conclusion: guessing at the bookmaker is worth less than watching the price.

We also tried **AI prediction**: injuries, motivation, form. Every point sounded convincing, and every one had long been priced into the odds. However lively the story, the line doesn't buy it.

After the detours, one plain truth remains:

> **Money shows where it's going; the line speaks.**
> But people watching the line get carried away easily: chasing favorites, fearing underdogs, shaky hands near kickoff. You can tell at a glance that emotion is doing the trading.

So we hand both the watching and the buying to machines, and keep only one thing for people: **discipline**.

## Three Informants, One Referee

**European odds** track market-wide odds movements: who has been collectively abandoned, who is quietly defending, and whether the draw line has been given up. This is the informant closest to the action.

**Asian handicap** tracks the line and the water (odds): sudden pivots near kickoff, big-money backing on the home side. Money thrown down in real cash is more honest than anything said out loud.

**Over/under** tracks the goal line. Once a goal-rich setup appears, the goal count for the match is often already foreshadowed.

Each of the three informants brings different news. When the news agrees, the referee is willing to make a call. **Matches where they disagree (European odds and Asian handicap contradicting each other) are simply not touched.** If the informants are already arguing among themselves, why would you bet at all?

## Discipline Matters More Than Vision

Once the direction is set, everything else is discipline:

- **No bets at low odds**: single-selection odds under 1.5, or double-selection odds below 1.3 after discounting. No matter how good the signal, it isn't bought. At odds that low, even a win doesn't earn much.
- **No bets without clear signals**: no signal, conflicting signals, or an ambiguous direction means waiting. Missing a bet costs nothing; a wrong bet does.
- **Quality determines stake size**: the stronger the signal, the larger the stake (1/2/4 units). No all-in gambling.
- **Bets are placed automatically 15 minutes before kickoff, and results are settled automatically when they come in**: no shaky hands near kickoff, no urge to raise stakes after a win or chase losses after a defeat.

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

This project is for data research only and does not constitute any purchase advice. Buy lottery tickets only at licensed physical retail outlets. Those under 18 years old may not participate.

## roscaelum Firewall

### What is this
A lightweight, simple, secure, and essential firewall that directly manipulates nftables via netlink.  
Under development.

### Design Principles

#### Simple and easy to use
All configuration is managed in YAML. No more mashing `ufw status`!  
It also runs as a single binary and does not depend on the `nft` command, so installation is easy.

#### Secure
It displays warnings for improper configurations. It is also written in memory-safe Go.

#### Many useful features
It includes features that help make servers more secure, such as allowing access only on specific interfaces or blocking access from arbitrary IPs.  
Want to build your own router? roscaelum includes features to help you set up a simple home router!  

#### Fully offline operation
Since it does not require communication with external APIs, rule generation and application can all be done offline.

### Usage
Note: Disable any existing firewall before use.

```
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nexryai/roscaelum/main/install.sh
sudo bash install.sh

# Edit the rules
sudo nano /etc/roscaelum.yml

# Apply
sudo rcfctl enable

# Apply automatically at startup
sudo systemctl enable roscaelum
```
#### Build from source
```
# Build
make

# Install
sudo make install
```

### Known issues
#### On RHEL-family systems, systemd complains with a Permission error
This is caused by SELinux.  
Resolve it with `sudo restorecon -R /usr/bin/rcfctl`.

#### Conflicts with Docker
You can work around it by setting `allowAllFwd` to true.

# Pier

A cross-device workbench for coding agents.

Pier is a cross-device workbench for coding agents. In a single interface, you can use the built-in [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) as well as [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com) and [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) installed on your computer. It centrally manages workspaces and sessions across multiple computers and provides file, Git, and terminal operations. Agents run resident on their own computers, and you can check progress, send instructions, and approve operations from the desktop or the phone.

## Features

- **One interface, three agents**: Built in pi, and drives Claude Code and Codex installed on the computer. Their sessions are shared with the CLI in the terminal, so you can continue at any time in the terminal with `claude --resume` / `codex resume`.
- **Unified management of multiple computers**: Each computer is a node. Paste a pairing link, or log in to a Linux computer over SSH to automatically install Pier and pair it. That computer's workspaces and sessions are listed in the sidebar alongside those of the local machine.
- **Follow up from your phone anytime**: The native app (Expo / React Native) pairs by scanning a QR code, then lets you check progress, send instructions, and approve operations. It reconnects automatically after a disconnection and resends missed messages.
- **A complete workbench**: File browsing, preview, and editing; Git (including worktrees); a built-in terminal; a remote browser; port forwarding; process management; scheduled tasks; Skills and MCP management; and voice input.
- **End-to-end encrypted remote access**: Paired connections are encrypted throughout. When devices are not on the same network, the connection goes through a self-hosted [Pier Relay](https://github.com/yiranxiaohui/Pier/blob/HEAD/apps/relay/README.md). It prefers direct P2P connections via hole punching, and the relay only sees ciphertext.
- **Hassle-free installation and updates**: Windows, macOS, and Linux all have installer packages and command-line install entry points. The desktop and Android apps support in-app updates (with signature verification and an optional mainland China acceleration route), and Linux servers can be installed as background services.
